issues.name: Trade and tariffs
issues.intro: Statements from the Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee's ranking member on tariffs and trade policy.

items.t: Responded to a threat to double tariffs on Mexico.
items.q: Tariffs should be a tool to level the playing field for American workers and businesses, not a weapon to scapegoat immigrants or settle political scores.

items.t: Joined Los Angeles County colleagues for a roundtable on trade policy at the Port of Los Angeles.
items.q: It’s clear that President Trump’s chaotic trade policies are hurting Americans

items.t: Criticized a round of tariffs the administration said were meant to combat forced labor.
items.q: We need to take forced labor seriously.

issues.name: Immigration and taxpayer data
issues.intro: A roll call on immigration enforcement and a court filing on IRS data shared with ICE.

items.t: Led a bicameral amicus brief on IRS-to-ICE taxpayer address sharing.
items.q: led 85 House and Senate Democrats in filing a bicameral amicus brief urging the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to uphold a lower court’s order blocking Immigration and Customs Enforcement from using – or even viewing – tens of thousands of taxpayers’ addresses obtained from the IRS

items.t: Voted against the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29). It passed 264–159.

issues.name: Health care and Medicaid
issues.intro: Roll calls on health care and Medicaid bills.

items.t: Voted against the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act (H.R. 498). It passed 215–201.
Voted against H.R. 1, the reconciliation bill the Clerk lists as the One Big Beautiful Act. It passed 215–214.

issues.name: Housing and Social Security
issues.intro: Bills the member introduced on rental housing and surviving-spouse Social Security benefits.

items.t: Introduced the Protecting Our Widows and Widowers in Retirement (POWR) Act.
items.q: After decades of hard work and paying into the system, widows and widowers deserve to keep the benefits they earned together.

items.t: Introduced the bipartisan Rental Housing Investment Act.
items.q: Southern California families are being priced out of their own communities

israel.question: Israel or Palestine?
israel.headline: Mixed
israel.headlineWhy: "Mixed" because the items point both ways: 1 toward conditions on offensive weapons for Israel and 1 toward continued defensive aid.
israel.summary: One statement so far, from the newest 30 releases: the member cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act, which covers offensive weapons only, and said defensive aid for close allies should continue.

items.t: Cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act, saying “I oppose providing offensive weapons to Prime Minister Netanyahu and his far-right government without meaningful safeguards or accountability.”
In the same statement: “While I have consistently supported defensive aid for close American allies, military aid for Israel must include strong conditions to prevent further suffering.”
